title: Surgical safety: the WHO checklist, NatSSIPs 2 and LocSSIPs

guidelineVersions: NPSA Patient Safety Alert: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (January 2009)

related.why: What to do when the checks reveal a wrong-site near miss
Duty of candour after a retained swab

brief.setting: Operating theatre, before the first case
brief.scenario: Mrs Gwen Tregarthen, 52, is first on the list for an elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The team is about to start the day.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the surgical safety checklist and the national and local safety standards for invasive procedures.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Three WHO pauses, then NatSSIPs 2's eight steps, then LocSSIPs, then why it works.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Reciting the checklist as a form rather than a team conversation anyone can stop.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The day starts with a team brief, then sign in, time out and sign out for each patient."

grid.label: Checklist structure
grid.fail: Cannot name the three phases or when they happen.
grid.pass: Sign in before induction; time out before skin incision; sign out before the patient leaves theatre; read aloud with the team.
grid.high: WHO introduced it in 2008; the NPSA adapted it for England and Wales in 2009 and required it for every patient.

grid.label: Sign in
grid.fail: Omits allergy, airway or blood loss risk.
grid.pass: Identity, site, procedure and consent; site marked; anaesthetic check; pulse oximeter; allergy; difficult airway or aspiration; blood loss over 500 ml.
grid.high: Knows the child threshold (7 ml/kg) and that a risk of blood loss means planning access and fluids.

grid.label: Time out
grid.fail: Treats time out as a formality or starts before the team is ready.
grid.pass: Introductions by name and role; patient, procedure and site; antibiotics within 60 minutes; anticipated critical events; imaging displayed.
grid.high: Adds the England and Wales prompts: VTE prophylaxis and the SSI bundle (warming, hair removal, glycaemic control).

grid.label: Sign out
grid.fail: Lets the patient leave before counts are confirmed.
grid.pass: Procedure recorded; instrument, swab and sharps counts complete; specimens labelled with the patient's name; equipment problems; key recovery concerns.
grid.high: Reads specimen labels aloud; knows NatSSIPs 2 makes reconciliation of items a standard of its own to prevent retained objects.

grid.label: NatSSIPs 2
grid.fail: Hasn't heard of NatSSIPs, or thinks it replaces the WHO checklist.
grid.pass: National standards (Centre for Perioperative Care, January 2023) for all invasive procedures, in or out of theatre, building on the WHO checklist.
grid.high: Names the eight sequential standards, from consent and procedural verification to handover and debrief, including safe and efficient use of implants and reconciliation of items.

grid.label: LocSSIPs
grid.fail: Cannot say what a LocSSIP is.
grid.pass: Local standard operating procedures written by the organisation from NatSSIPs 2 for a procedure or area, e.g. ward chest drains.
grid.high: Adds the organisational standards: senior leadership, team training, and governance focused on improvement; patients involved in the checks.

grid.label: Why it matters
grid.pass: Improves teamwork and catches errors; in the WHO pilot, deaths fell from 1.5% to 0.8% and complications from 11% to 7%.
grid.high: Knows the benefit depends on genuine engagement: anyone can stop the procedure, compliance and quality are audited, and debriefs feed learning.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Three pauses read aloud with the team: sign in before induction, time out before skin incision, and sign out before the patient leaves theatre.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Identity, site, procedure and consent; site marked; anaesthetic machine and drug check; pulse oximeter on; allergies; difficult airway or aspiration risk; and risk of blood loss over 500 ml.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Everyone introduces themselves by name and role. We confirm the patient, procedure and site, antibiotics within 60 minutes, critical events from each discipline, and that imaging is displayed.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Confirm the procedure recorded, instrument, swab and sharps counts complete, specimens labelled with her name, any equipment problems, and key concerns for recovery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The National Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures, updated by the Centre for Perioperative Care in January 2023. They cover all invasive procedures, in or out of theatre, and build on the WHO checklist.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A local procedure written by the trust from NatSSIPs 2, for example for chest drains on the ward.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It improves team communication. In the WHO pilot, deaths fell from 1.5% to 0.8% and complications from 11% to 7%.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: WHO introduced it in 2008. The NPSA adapted it for England and Wales in 2009 and required it for every surgical patient, including under local anaesthesia.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What's the blood loss threshold in a child?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Seven ml per kg. If there's a risk, we plan adequate access and fluids before starting.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The England and Wales version also asks about VTE prophylaxis and the SSI bundle: warming, hair removal and glycaemic control.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Specimen labels are read aloud. NatSSIPs 2 makes reconciliation of items a separate standard, to prevent retained foreign objects.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Consent and procedural verification, team brief, sign in, time out, safe and efficient use of implants, reconciliation of items, sign out, and handover and debrief.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What does NatSSIPs ask of the organisation?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Senior clinical leadership, time for team training, and governance focused on improvement. Patients should be involved in the checks too.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: So why does it sometimes fail?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: When it's done as a tick box. It works when anyone feels able to stop the procedure, when we audit quality not just completion, and when debriefs feed learning.

failures.move: Letting the patient leave before counts are confirmed.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: a retained swab or instrument can go unnoticed.

failures.move: Doing time out while starting the operation.
failures.consequence: Wrong-site or wrong-patient errors are no longer caught.

failures.move: Believing NatSSIPs replaces the WHO checklist.
failures.consequence: Misses that NatSSIPs builds on it and extends to procedures outside theatre.
Signals poor safety culture, the reason checks fail.

recovery.line: Patient, site, anaesthetic safety, then the three risks: allergy, airway, blood loss.
NatSSIPs 2 applies to all invasive procedures, supported by a local LocSSIP.

knowledge.fact: Sign in before induction; time out before skin incision; sign out before the patient leaves theatre.
Time out: antibiotic prophylaxis within the last 60 minutes; England and Wales version adds VTE and SSI bundle prompts.
NatSSIPs 2 (CPOC, January 2023): eight sequential standards plus organisational standards; LocSSIPs are local procedures based on it.
WHO pilot: deaths 1.5% to 0.8%, complications 11% to 7%.

recall.think: Wrong site, wrong patient, retained items.
recall.say: "Anyone can stop the procedure if a check isn't right."

numbers.meaning: antibiotics before incision, checked at time out
blood loss risk flagged at sign in

recall.trap: Treating the checklist as the nurse's form.
recall.finish: Debrief and handover, with learning fed back.

sources.name: World Health Organization. Surgical Safety Checklist
sources.supports: Sign in before induction (identity, site, procedure, consent; site marked; anaesthesia check; pulse oximeter; allergy; difficult airway/aspiration; blood loss >500 ml, 7 ml/kg in children); time out before skin incision (introductions, patient, procedure, incision site; antibiotics within 60 minutes; anticipated critical events; imaging); sign out before leaving theatre (procedure, counts, specimen labels read aloud with patient name, equipment problems, recovery concerns); local modification encouraged

sources.name: National Patient Safety Agency. Patient Safety Alert: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (NPSA/2009/PSA002/U1)
sources.supports: WHO launched Safe Surgery Saves Lives in June 2008; checklist adapted for England and Wales and required for every patient undergoing a surgical procedure, including under local anaesthesia; time out adds VTE prophylaxis and SSI bundle (antibiotics within 60 minutes, warming, hair removal, glycaemic control)

sources.name: World Health Organization. Global guidelines for the prevention of surgical site infection
sources.supports: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision, considering the half-life of the antibiotic

sources.name: Centre for Perioperative Care. National Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures 2 (NatSSIPs 2)
sources.supports: Revision of the 2015 NatSSIPs; applies to all invasive procedures in all settings; organisational standards (leadership, team training, improvement-focused governance) and eight sequential standards (consent and procedural verification, team brief, sign in, time out, safe and efficient use of implants, reconciliation of items to prevent retained foreign objects, sign out, handover/debrief) extending the WHO five steps; LocSSIPs as local procedures based on NatSSIPs 2; patient involvement

sources.name: Haynes AB, Weiser TG, Berry WR, et al. A surgical safety checklist to reduce morbidity and mortality in a global population. N Engl J Med 2009;360:491–9
sources.supports: Deaths 1.5% to 0.8% and inpatient complications 11.0% to 7.0% after checklist introduction in eight hospitals

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; examiner-led questioning in applied knowledge stations

partner.opening: Mrs Tregarthen is first on the list for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Tell me about the WHO surgical safety checklist.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about allergies at sign in
reveals.finding: She reports a penicillin allergy (rash) not on the drug chart. Expected action: record it on the drug chart and allergy wristband, and discuss with the anaesthetist before the antibiotic choice (cefuroxime has been given).

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about antibiotics at time out
reveals.finding: Cefuroxime was given 90 minutes ago in the anaesthetic room before a delay.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the count at sign out
reveals.finding: Scrub practitioner reports one swab unaccounted for.

push.question: When is each phase done?
push.expect: Before induction, before incision, before leaving theatre.

push.question: What is checked at time out?
push.expect: Introductions, patient/procedure/site, antibiotics within 60 min, critical events, imaging.

push.question: How is NatSSIPs 2 different?
push.expect: National standards for all invasive procedures; eight steps building on WHO.

curveballs.prompt: At sign out, one swab is missing.
curveballs.safeAnswer: The patient doesn't leave: recount, search the field and patient, and X-ray if still missing; document and report.

curveballs.prompt: The anaesthetist is about to do a nerve block. Any extra check?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop Before You Block: confirm the side and site immediately before needle insertion.

curveballs.prompt: The antibiotic was given 90 minutes ago.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Flag it at time out and confirm with the anaesthetist. WHO (2016) accepts prophylaxis within 120 minutes before incision, so no automatic redose; follow local policy.
